fields.text: Antisocial pyromancer, quick to anger

fields.label: Description
fields.text: Home life is quasi-nonexistent — parents killed by adventurers shortly after his birth. Ran from foster homes but keeps going to school because it's the one thing he's good at. Deals weed to get by, in too deep with bad people. Believes some things must be destroyed for better things to grow.

fields.label: Hook
fields.text:
Sesh 8 answers his backstory: Edward is his father. Bix believes his parents were killed by adventurers shortly after his birth — but he was too young to remember and has only ever had rumours. The truth is that his mother Goblinenon was killed clearing squatters out of this house, his father was dying beside her, and the vampires turned him to save him. Edward carried the baby down to town that same night and left him there on purpose.

His own mansion night still stands: he broke in one rainy night after running from a foster home and saw spooky shit (Sesh 5). Sesh 6's unused thread — his account is incomplete, and a diary in the house fills the gap — is still on the table and now has an obvious thing to be about.

Play him not knowing. The reveal is paced across the whole night: the glimmer, then being watched, then the photograph, and Edward does not explain himself until the epilogue. Nothing forces it early.

fields.label: Description
fields.text: A crafty, petty schemer who idolizes mob bosses despite a wholesome family. Hustler who loves money, smart but not bookish — one teacher genuinely believes in him and he wavers between the street life and escaping to college. Sells cigarettes in the school bathroom.

fields.label: Hook
fields.text:
Ex-member of the Bad Kids crew. Fell out with Poe Boy over uneven cuts of their silly-bandz racket. As a kid the crew threw rocks at the mansion windows on dares — one Halloween, something went wrong.

He owns the house. His great-uncle Vinny won it off Orlok at cards on 14 November 1931, and the settlement they drafted — drunk, at four in the morning — vests title in whoever holds the marker. Vinny pressed that poker chip into a twelve-year-old's palm after hearing the kid had a racket going, and never explained what it was. It has been in Julia's pocket since session one.

fields.label: Finale
fields.text:
Quiet and overlooked to head of household. He finds the study alone, works out what he is holding, and then has to say it out loud in a ballroom full of people who have never once looked at him: “This is my house.” Nobody believes him — including his own party — so Orlok has to confirm it in front of every teenager in Transyltown. Then the renewal, plain, at the threshold: “You can stay.”

Epilogue: he leads the gang and fronts for the vampires as the one who can stand in daylight. He takes no rent and asks nothing — same as Vinny. Then he calls a nursing home. Sesh 8

fields.label: Description
fields.text: Worships the Devil — who appears as an all-black goat with an upside-down red cross on its face — and draws magic from that worship. Regular-degular atheist suburban family thinks it's a phase. Frequent detention regular after the principal catches her doing spells on school grounds.

fields.label: Hook
fields.text:
Funds the tour fund by charging classmates for love spells and revenge spells. The money lives in a goat-shaped piggy bank — she has been feeding coins to a goat for years.

Sesh 8 gives her the mansion connection: she sold the dead kid the love spell. He paid her for a wishing willow and wrote I want Angelique to notice me on it. It worked. Angelique noticed him — and when Poe Boy went looking for someone who knew the kid well enough to flirt convincingly, Angelique was the one who could. The willow is still in his backpack upstairs.

Her choice is the second ask. After the recording is safely on the drive, the Spirit asks to be moved somewhere safe. It is far past her level; her patron can lend her the power and names a price — everything in the piggy bank, the whole concert fund. Nothing plot-critical hangs on her yes (see the Spirit's card), which is what makes it a real choice.

fields.label: Finale
fields.text: She gets the concert anyway. Poe Boy loves the same satanic metal band and had tickets. When his mother arrives in the driveway she grounds him — and he is certainly not going to that satan concert — and the tickets end up with Simone, who spent every dollar she had a few hours earlier. Sesh 8

fields.label: Name
fields.text: Great Uncle Vinny

fields.label: Subtitle
fields.text: Won the house in 1931

fields.label: Role
fields.text: Backstory NPC · alive

fields.label: Field · Race
fields.text: Gnome

fields.label: Field · Trade
fields.text: Untaxed cigarettes & bootleg liquor

fields.label: Field · Status
fields.text: Alive, ancient, in a home

fields.label: Description
fields.text:
Gnomey's great-uncle. Ran cigarettes and liquor on the back roads at night through Prohibition. Nobody in the family thinks he's anything. He needed somewhere to keep the liquor, and there was exactly one building in the county nobody would ever search — so he walked up the hill and asked, which nobody had done in two hundred years.

The deal: Orlok gets the cellar filled and takes a case a month off the top. Liquor turns out to be one of the only human things that still works on a vampire — the one pleasure he has left. Every month Vinny comes up with the delivery, they crack a bottle, and they play cards.

fields.label: Hook
fields.text:
14 November 1931. Orlok goes down, keeps playing to get it back, goes further down, and by four in the morning the only thing he has left worth anything is the house. They draft the settlement drunk. Vinny walks out with one blue chip — and then lets them stay, rent-free, in writing, forever. That's the family principle in full: you always collect, and then you're not a bastard about it.

Years later he hears a twelve-year-old relative had a little operation going and blew it up rather than eat a skim. He drives over that week:

“Twelve years old and he's got a crew.”
“I don't have a crew anymore.”
“You'll get another one.” — and he presses the chip into the kid's palm.

fields.label: Finale
fields.text: He is alive and mostly gone, which is why nobody could ever explain the chip. The last beat of the campaign is a phone call to his home: “Uncle Vinny. It's me. I collected.” Sesh 8

fields.label: Name
fields.text: The Devil (Goat)

fields.label: Subtitle
fields.text: Simone's patron

fields.label: Role
fields.text: Otherworldly patron

fields.label: Field · Form
fields.text: All-black goat, upside-down red cross

fields.label: Description
fields.text: Source of Simone's warlock power — and, per Sesh 8, the only thing in the house that can move a soul out of a machine. It cannot do the work itself: it appears, it lends her the power, and it names a price.

fields.label: Hook
fields.text:
The price is the concert fund — the goat-shaped piggy bank, smashed. Her patron's price is, functionally, itself. If she pays, she performs the ritual that moves the Spirit into the USB; if she doesn't, the party still leaves with everything they need and the kid stays where he is.

The Spirit can see it and she can't. He has been in that room for years and he notices it the moment it arrives — that is how the offer reaches the table.

It joins the AIM chat. The prop turns into a three-way chat room the moment it arrives: the window's whole theme flips to oxblood and black, the buddy bar reads l0stsignal99, GOAT, and every sound it makes is a stock AIM clip pitched down and distorted. It types in serif, in capitals, with full stops — the only participant in that window who was not raised on a keyboard. It gets no typing indicator; it does not compose, it arrives.

Voicing it: it will not explain. Asked what it wants the money for, it says No. and nothing else. That refusal is the whole point — a stated reason would make this a transaction, and it needs to be a leap.

fields.label: Epilogue
fields.text: It does not leave her. Whichever way she decides, its last line before it signs off is that it will still be there on Monday. If she paid, it adds the one crack in it: She will not get that money back. I want her to hear me say so. I did not take it to be cruel. Deliberately ambiguous — it needed the money, or it was keeping her out of something. Play whichever you two prefer; the prop doesn't decide.

fields.label: Name
fields.text: DJ Poe Boy

fields.label: Subtitle
fields.text: The Big Bad

fields.label: Role
fields.text: Antagonist · Ringleader

fields.label: Field · Race
fields.text: Kenku

fields.label: Field · Class
fields.text: Bard — College of Glamour

fields.label: Field · Alignment
fields.text: Chaotic Neutral

fields.label: Field · Type
fields.text: ENFJ

fields.label: Description
fields.text: Way-too-cool-for-school personified: obnoxiously subversive, but with real underground cred. Ambitious and callous to the edge of psychopathy — not sadistic, just indifferent to suffering if it serves the work. Charismatic, subtly manipulative. Emancipated rich kid, deeply insecure about his upper-class parents who adore him anyway.

fields.label: Hook
fields.text:
The plan: invite them, lock them in, and sample the screams of real beings terrorized by real monsters for his horror score. He met the vampires by accident while recording spooky noises in the house, sold them a plan to scare off the mega-mall developers, then tested it on one kid — and found out he doesn't stop. Candidate embarrassing real name: Upton Maximillion Livingsworth III (floated in Sesh 3 as a joke, never locked).

His AIM account is saved on the machine upstairs — DJPoeBoy187 — and his password is his cat. Fluffy123. The party finds it on a sticky note and spends the whole Spirit conversation typing as him. It is the same joke as the Volvo: the most feared kid in Transyltown is a boy with a house cat and parents who adore him.

Playing him: Kenku speak only in sounds recorded from others — a DJ who samples voices, whose crime is trapping a kid's voice in a machine, cannot speak in one of his own. Sesh 8: “Voice him in borrowed lines.” Glamour supplies the charm that holds the crew.

fields.label: Finale
fields.text:
He charms the crowd. An Enthralling Performance holds the 3AM audience where he wants them — he needs them frightened and he needs them to stay, so the charm is part of the crime. He sets the vampires on the party with the lie that killed the kid, tries to recruit the developer and gets brushed off, then spends phase three casting Command — “Drop.” — to keep the USB off his decks. He is not killed. He is un-performed: the recording plays in full, the glamour breaks, one boo becomes the whole room, Dracula takes his mic, his Command stops landing — and his parents pull into the drive and call him Upton.

Sesh 8's last turn of the knife: he loves the same satanic metal band Simone has been saving all year for, and he had tickets. His mother grounds him in front of the entire school — and he is certainly not going to that satan concert. The tickets go to Simone. the 24 Aug doc paste + Sesh 8

fields.label: Description
fields.text: Dumb as bricks but genuinely charming — a hustler who isn't conniving. Into the dumbest conspiracy theories. The one crew member who needs no manipulation: he just wants to help his best friend, not knowing he's being used.

fields.label: Hook
fields.text:
Makes music with Poe Boy — they're tight. The doc ties him to Julia's cigarette trade as the school kingpin, which is how Gnomey's world overlaps his.

His arc, per Sesh 8: “Sworn to a liar without knowing it. His oath breaks when he believes us about the kid.” He is the only member of the crew whose turn is mechanical as well as emotional — put the moment he believes the players somewhere the table can see it land.

Oath of Devotion fits because the doc already makes him honest to a fault and genuinely wanting to help the friend who is using him. His race is one of the two blanks Sesh 8 leaves open, alongside Simone's.

fields.label: Finale
fields.text: Sesh 8 gave him the oathbreak; the 24 Aug doc paste gives it a trigger. He stands on the decks in phase three and his Aura of Protection buffs Poe Boy's saves, so the party's control spells bounce until they deal with him — a puzzle, not a wall. He is the only person in the room who isn't charmed. He never needed to be; he just believes his friend, which is exactly why it hurts. Then the recording plays and the oath breaks with no saving throw: Devotion's first tenet is don't lie or cheat, and there is no save against hearing your best friend stay calm while a kid dies. He stops fighting and sits down. On Monday he records a diss track — sincere, terrible, devastating. Sesh 8 + the 24 Aug doc paste

fields.label: Canon note (not player-facing)

fields.label: Role

fields.label: Field · Class

fields.label: Field · Vibe
fields.text: Trad goth, nihilist with a soft spot

fields.label: Description
fields.text:
More authentically goth than Poe Boy — existential, hedonist, 'any second could be my last.' Smart but unsure of herself; Poe Boy exploits her low self-worth. If anyone can be pulled out of his orbit, it's her.

Changeling Rogue, per Sesh 8 — “No fixed face, which is how you wrote her. Useful the second she flips.”

fields.label: Hook
fields.text:
She tries to warn them at the gazebo and can't — Sesh 5, because the rest of the crew is standing right there. Play it as a look, a half-sentence, something swallowed. It makes her “get down” at the mansion a second attempt rather than a first contact, and the players will already have clocked her trying to say something.

She typed some of the fake screen-name messages that lured the first kid to the mansion — she thought it was a prank. When he stopped coming to school she started to suspect. She's at the mansion the night of the party to find out for herself, which is why she's already inside and is the first to find the heroes and tell them to hide. She can't say any of it out loud: accusing Poe Boy means admitting her part.

Sesh 8 explains the pull. Before any of it, the kid paid Simone for a love spell — I want Angelique to notice me — and it worked. She noticed him, which is exactly why she was the one who could write to him convincingly, and she played along. Nobody ever cancelled it. She still notices him, and the compulsion's object is a boy who is not anywhere any more, so it reads as a pull toward the house he is actually in. That is what she is following the night of the party.

She is not off the hook. The spell only ever made her notice. It didn't make her cruel, it didn't type for her, and it didn't drive her out here. Everything she did with the noticing was hers.

fields.label: Name
fields.text: Dood Mansion

fields.label: Subtitle
fields.text: The haunted house

fields.label: Role
fields.text: Primary location

fields.label: Field · Name
fields.text: 'Dood' = dead (Dutch)

fields.label: Field · History
fields.text: Abandoned Dutch mansion on the edge of town

fields.label: Description
fields.text:
Where the whole back half plays out. The front door has been boarded for decades — until the night of the party, when the boards come off and are stacked against the porch rail. That un-boarding is the only visible change to the house, and it's the invitation. Once they're inside, the doors bolt shut. Rooms are built around puzzles and one combat set-piece, ending in the food-stash reveal and a hidden room.

Two of Poe Boy's setups, not one. The old room upstairs holds his original recording rig and the computer the kid is inside — he hasn't been back in it (Sesh 7). The ballroom is the show he's built for tonight, wired to speakers through the rest of the house, and it's where the climax happens. The power is hot-wired off the neighbouring property — which is also the one thread anyone outside the house could pull on.

fields.label: Hook
fields.text:
Rumored haunted because of the vampires. A real-estate company wants to demolish it for a mega mall, and has knocked in daylight several times — when the vampires can't answer the door or defend themselves at all.

Orlok built it, lost it at cards in 1931, and has needed someone else's permission to live in it ever since. It does not belong to the vampires and has not for seventy years.

Rooms Sesh 8 puts on the map:
· The study — sealed since the thirties. A poker set exactly one chip short, the last hand still on the table, and a strongbox holding the deed and the signed settlement. Gnomey's room.
· The party room — the night Edward and Goblinenon's cart broke down and they found two vampires partying. Bottles, a record still on the turntable, forty years of dust on somebody's good night. Where Bix finds the photograph.
· The cellar — Vinny's liquor went in here from 1920 and repeal came in '33 and he never came back for it, so a wall of crates is still down there. It is also where the animals are kept, which is what the food-stash puzzle reveals.
· The old rig upstairs — the computer, the Spirit, the backpack.
· The ballroom — tonight's show and the climax.

fields.label: Finale
fields.text: the 24 Aug doc paste runs the back half as one line with no fork: locked in, one Saturday fight, the Spirit and the USB upstairs, the food stash, then 3AM and three phases with no break. Sesh 8 cut the corridor set-piece and added the study and the party room in its place. The two-setups decision pays off directly — the Spirit is in the old rig upstairs and the aux is on the ballroom decks, so the finale's objective is a journey across the map. the 24 Aug doc paste

fields.label: Canon note (not player-facing)
fields.text:
Ratified by Scott: 'Dood' is both — the builder's family surname and the Dutch pun, so Cornelis Dood is a real person in the fiction. That also answers Spencer's Sesh 6 'lmk if thats too dumb lol' about the mansion name.

And as of 31 Aug, Cornelis Dood is Orlok. Sesh 8 makes Orlok the man who built this house; Dood is his mortal surname. The town buried him and he never left, which is why the Crier's obituary is technically accurate. Not in the Google Doc yet.

fields.text: Vamp: Orlok

fields.label: Subtitle
fields.text: True-to-folklore

fields.label: Role
fields.text: Vampire (secretly good)

fields.label: Field · Style
fields.text: Nosferatu / Count Orlok

fields.label: Description
fields.text: The genuinely eerie one, straight from folklore. Like the others, actually harmless to the heroes — they live off small animals and want to be left alone.

fields.label: Hook
fields.text:
He built this house. Never married, no children, alone in forty rooms — Sesh 6's description of the original owner, now spent on him. He was dying by his own hand when Dracula turned up uninvited and wouldn't take no for an answer, so the one he cannot stand is the one he owes his existence to.

Then he lost it at cards. A gnome bootlegger named Vinny came up the hill around the turn of the century wanting cellar space, and they ended up playing every month for decades. On 14 November 1931 Orlok went down, kept playing, and put the house up because it was the only thing left. They never spoke again — not from hatred, from shame.

Playing him: patience, not menace. Impeccable courtesy, especially while doing something appalling. He explains his reasoning to people he is about to hurt. He will not say a bad word about Vinny.

fields.label: Finale
fields.text:
Mechanically incapable of killing a PC in first contact and in phase one — grapple, shove, frighten, never Bite on a conscious creature. A the 24 Aug doc paste rule, not DM mercy, so the mechanics are themselves the clue.

He is the boss, and it costs one syllable. When Dracula gets carried away with the party, Orlok ends it with a single word and nobody speaks until he is finished. Then the dismissal: “The night is young. It would be terribly rude to be finished with you already. Go on. Have a look around. We'll find you when we're ready.” — every word of which is a threat to the party and an accurate description of a haunted-house attraction to him.

And at the end he has to confirm the gnome's claim out loud, to a room full of teenagers. He is pissed, he complies perfectly, and he thanks him through his teeth. the 24 Aug doc paste + Sesh 8

fields.label: Canon note (not player-facing)
fields.text: 'Does most of the actual frightening on Poe Boy's say-so' was a codex invention. Ratified by Scott, 31 Aug: Cornelis Dood is Orlok. Dood is his mortal surname — he built the house, the Dutch pun survives, the puzzle prop survives, and the Crier's obituary is technically accurate. The town really did bury him. 31 Aug · not in doc

fields.text: He is the one who lays hands on the party. When the stealth finally fails on Saturday night he swoops in and grapples, pushes and shoves — enjoying it far too much and doing no damage. Then Orlok says one word and he stops instantly. That single exchange establishes the whole hierarchy without a fight.

fields.label: Finale
fields.text: He gets the campaign's biggest laugh and its cleanest catharsis. When the recording finishes and the room wakes up, Dracula seizes the mic and denounces Poe Boy magnificently — he has waited all night for a real audience. The crowd cheers, and plenty still aren't sure it isn't part of the show. Also bound by the no-Bite rule in phase one. the 24 Aug doc paste

fields.text: Exactly what it says on the tin, and Sesh 8 makes him the answer to Bix's whole backstory. All three vampires want the same thing — to be left alone — and all three believe the kid who came up the hill that night ran off out a window. Nobody has told them he died, or that Poe Boy has had him in a machine ever since.

fields.label: Hook
fields.text:
How he got here. Originally the house was just Orlok and Dracula. On a rainy night Edward and Goblinenon — Bix's mother — were passing through town when their cart threw a tire, and they knocked at the nearest big house looking for help. What they found was two vampires having a party, Rocky Horror style. They had such a good time that they gave up the nomadic life and squatted here. About nine months later, Bix was born.

Around that time the real-estate company hired men to clear the squatters and the vampires out. Goblinenon was killed and Edward was badly hurt; the vampires turned him to save his life. He woke up as a vampire, was horrified at what he was, and carried the baby down into town in the middle of the night — because anything was better than being raised by a single father who was now a monster.

Playing him tonight: he knows exactly who Bix is and has known since the party walked in. He watches and does not approach. Let him be caught at it twice before anyone gets an explanation.

fields.label: Finale
fields.text: Bound by the no-Bite rule in phase one. All three turn the moment the developer dies — the party killed the man taking their home, in front of them, so it costs no persuasion check. Then they fight alongside the party: roughly three extra level-5 bodies, which is why phase three is a catharsis rather than a hard fight. the 24 Aug doc paste

fields.text: It does two jobs at once. It proves the house is dangerous after an evening in which nothing has actually hurt anyone, and it plants that the dangerous things in this building are human-made — which is the thesis the computer room pays off the next day. The party has no way to know whose it is yet.

fields.label: Canon note (not player-facing)
fields.text:
The doc names it and nothing else. That it is Poe Boy's, what it is, what it does, and every number behind it are codex proposals. See the Combat tab for the budget.

It replaces the Gjenganger, which Sesh 8 retired by displacement: Orlok took the lonely-original-owner backstory, and the corridor set-piece the creature was going to fill was cut. fields.label: Description
fields.text: A kid from school, lured to the mansion by a fake AIM screen name as Poe Boy's test run. The vampires chased him exactly as agreed; he broke for the one lit room, got to the keyboard and started typing for help. Poe Boy saw the open AIM window, shut the door and held it. Then he panicked over the body and cast a half-understood soul cage with no vessel prepared — so the machine still recording him took all of him.

fields.label: Hook
fields.text: Biggest clue in the house: he was killed by a human, not a monster — the thread that exonerates the vampires. He can name Poe Boy.

fields.label: Finale
fields.text:
He arms the party. He asks them to fetch his backpack, still in that room after all these years. Inside are two things: the thumb drive, and the wishing willow he bought from Simone when they were twelve. They plug the drive into the machine and it mounts under his name — which is the moment Simone and Angelique work out that this is the same boy. He uploads the recording of his own death over AIM's file-transfer window: scream_test_03_GOOD.wav, a filename Poe Boy chose, which the kid has had to look at every time the monitor wakes up. His first ask isn't directions — it's expose him. Hand the players a real USB stick.

Then Sesh 8's second ask: can you get me out of here. Not alive — out of the machine, into the drive, somewhere safe. Simone can't do it at her level; her patron can, for the price of her concert fund. This is deliberately not how the party gets the recording — the file is already on the drive before he asks, so a no costs them nothing but him. Say the no-path out loud in your own head before you run it: they still win, the machine simply goes dark at sunrise.

If she pays, the ritual runs in the AIM prop and looks like an ordinary file transfer until the progress bar exceeds its own boundaries. the 24 Aug doc paste + Sesh 8

fields.label: Epilogue
fields.text: He gets a job. Sesh 8: the kid's spirit ends up uploaded to the library computers, where he helps people find new books to read. The boy who died alone in a room nobody visited spends his afterlife in the one building in town that is always full of people looking for something. Sesh 8

fields.text: The AIM prop gives him voice and texture that the doc doesn't: the screen names l0stsignal99 and SmiLeyGrrL03, 'third locker from the end by the gym,' 'he just called me the test.' The prop also assumes he labelled the drive himself in a school computer lab, which is how it comes to carry his name.

fields.label: Description
fields.text: He wants to demolish the house and build a mega mall. His daytime visits are why the vampires went looking for a human ally at all — sunlight leaves them unable to answer the door or defend themselves. the 24 Aug doc paste promoted him from a background company to the third faction. He is an abjurer: not a fireball man, a man who solves problems by sealing them. He didn't dispute the 1937 article, he set a trap in the binding and had it cut to pieces — and he did it himself, which is why there is no contractor for the party to trace.

fields.label: Hook
fields.text:
Sesh 8 makes this company the reason Bix is an orphan. The men who cleared the squatters out of the mansion — killing Goblinenon and leaving Edward dying — were hired by this same real-estate company (confirmed by Scott, 30 Aug). It has been trying to take this house for about twenty years, which means the vampires' fear of it is not paranoia and Edward has a second reason to be in that driveway when it dies.

The party summons him and never finds out. Springing the trap on the Crier volume tells him someone has been in his records, and he drives out that night to see who. He does not know what is in the house — and that's better. He isn't amazed. Within four seconds it stops being folklore and becomes a contamination problem on a site he has already paid for, and he starts giving orders. Resolution beat unchanged: the company is scared off the land by the end (Sesh 5).

fields.label: Finale
fields.text: He breaches at 3AM and seals the exits behind him, his own crew included. Three sides, nobody sharing a goal. The only lethal fight of the finale — ~CR 5 plus six thugs, 2,400 XP against a 2,500 ceiling. He is the one death in the story and the only one who isn't a monster: self-defence, since he sealed them in and attacked first, but these are teenagers and it needs its silence before the comedy starts. His death is what flips the vampires, with no persuasion check. the 24 Aug doc paste

fields.label: Canon note (not player-facing)
fields.text:
The name is a proposal, not a decision. Ostrander is a genuine Hudson Valley Dutch surname — it sounds like a sign on a construction fence and quietly rhymes with the town's history without being a joke. It appears on the checkout card in the puzzle prop as W. Ostrander, so changing it means editing there too. Still open: company or family trust.

Also codex-side: three men in this house solve their problems by shutting something — the house bolts its doors, Poe Boy held one on a boy who was begging, and Ostrander's answer to a newspaper and a room full of witnesses is the same.

fields.label: Scene title
fields.text: History class

fields.label: Body
fields.text:
The super-seniors get grouped for a local-history / folklore project. This is the motivation to investigate — and the bookend they'll return to at the end to 'present their oral project.'

Why these five are in a room together: senior skip day, and nobody told them. Spencer floated it in the Sesh 1 comments and Scott took it — “Senior skip day except nobody told them. Then they kinda band together breakfast club vibes.” It earns the island-of-misfit-toys premise in one line, and it means being singled out as a group has already happened to them once before any card shows up in a locker.

fields.label: Bridge · read-aloud cue
fields.text: That’s the bell. You’ve got about four minutes to hit your locker and get to next period.

fields.label: Bridge · DM note
fields.text: Ends the scene on a clock, not a decision — nobody has to agree to anything for the story to move. Land the assignment constraint on the way out (a primary source, not the internet) so the Hall of Records is already on the board before anyone sees a card.

fields.label: Scene title
fields.text: Letters in the lockers

fields.label: Body
fields.text: Everyone finds a mysterious invitation to a haunted house at the abandoned Dutch mansion. Ooo, spooky.

fields.label: Bridge · read-aloud cue
fields.text: It’s barely noon. The card says seven. And not one of you has ever heard the name Dood before.

fields.label: Bridge · DM note
fields.text: Hours to kill plus a name nobody recognises is the itch; the class project is the excuse. Let them ask around if they want to — nobody else got a card, and finding that out is the strongest push toward town there is. If they march straight up the hill instead, the front is still boarded at this hour and bounces them back — which is the point. Anyone who goes early has seen the boards on. They come off during the day.

fields.label: Fallbacks · label
fields.text: If they don’t bite, hand a detour to a PC

fields.label: Fallback 1 · Bix says
fields.text: You’re in that library most days anyway. If anyone in this town knows a name that old, it’s the Records Keeper.

fields.label: Fallback 1 · why
fields.text: The library is already his routine, so the records hall is somewhere he’d suggest rather than be talked into.

fields.label: Fallback 2 · Gnomey says
fields.text: Your old crew’s at the gazebo, same as every day. If anything’s happening at that house, they’ll already know about it.

fields.label: Fallback 2 · why
fields.text: Sesh 3 puts the bad kids at a gazebo near the school — the crew is the lead, and Gnomey is the one who knows where to find them. He fell out with Poe Boy over the silly-bandz cuts, so making the suggestion costs him something.

fields.label: Scene title
fields.text: Town detours

fields.label: Body
fields.text:
The first third-to-half of Session 1. Two key stops: the Library / Hall of Records (Frisian lore + the vampire-slaying method + the Harbinger's warning) and the Gazebo near the school where the Bad Kids smoke — where they meet DJ Poe Boy and his entourage, and where Angelique tries to warn them and can't because the rest of the crew is standing right there.

What Poe Boy hands them here. He can’t help showing off, and every piece of it is a confession he doesn’t know he’s making:
· “I spin up there sometimes.” Sesh 3, verbatim. Explains why an abandoned house has gear in it, and it’s the first thing they’ll remember when they find the setup.
· “Wait till you see what I’ve done with the ballroom.” He’s proud of the venue and wants an audience for it. Puts the climax on the board hours early, from his own mouth.
· “Stick around till three.” Plants the flyer’s 3AM in person, from the host, so the timer is his voice and not a prop.

The tell is what he leaves out. He talks about the ballroom and never once mentions the other room he keeps gear in — the one upstairs he hasn’t been back into. Nobody notices at the gazebo. They notice at scene 7.

And the records hall is where Saturday's fight is. The bound volume is intact when she hands it over. Opening it springs Ostrander's trap — a swarm of index cards, a book cart, and two pairs of archival shears that ignore the party entirely and go for the article. By the time the shears are down the page is in pieces, which is where the torn-page prop comes from. Two shears means two approach lanes to body-block, and the number of cuts they get in decides how bad the puzzle is (500 XP). In the back pocket: a checkout card with four names, one of them Poe Boy's real one.

fields.label: Bridge · read-aloud cue
fields.text: Whoever’s wearing a watch — it’s ten to seven. That’s the time on the card.

fields.label: Bridge · DM note
fields.text:
A clock nudge, not a crowd. What’s waiting at the top of the hill: empty road, no cars, no light in any window — and the boards are off the front door, pried away and stacked neat against the porch rail. That is the only thing about this house that has changed in decades, and it is the invitation. The emptiness is the wrongness: no line to join and no social default to hide behind, so going in is curiosity and the assignment and nothing else.

And they've already summoned the villain without knowing it. Springing the trap told Ostrander someone has been in his records. He's in his car. Nobody at the table finds out until 3AM.

fields.label: Bridge · open question
fields.text: This reverses the 24 Aug doc paste twice — town is no longer combat-free, and Saturday's fight is no longer in the mansion. The mansion's fight moves to early Sunday.

fields.label: Scene title
fields.text: Enter Dood Mansion

fields.label: Body
fields.text: They go in out of pure curiosity, through a front door that has stood boarded for decades and isn’t any more — and the doors bolt shut behind them. Everything from here plays out inside. (Card says 7PM sharp; the DJ show flyer says 3AM — eight hours of house between them.)

fields.label: Bridge · read-aloud cue
fields.text: That’s a bolt throwing behind you. Footsteps overhead — and a hand comes out of the dark, grabs your sleeve, and pulls you down. It’s Angelique.

fields.label: Bridge · DM note
fields.text: Angelique reaching them first and telling them to hide is doc (Sesh 5; Sesh 7 explains why she’s in the house at all). Don’t let her explain yet. “Hiding from what” is the investigation’s first question, and she’s worth far more as a frightened stranger who won’t say why she came than as an exposition tap. She’ll answer eventually — make them earn it.

fields.label: Fallbacks · label
fields.text: If they try to walk straight back out

fields.label: Fallback 1 · The door says
fields.text: It doesn’t move. And there’s no bolt on your side to throw.

fields.label: Fallback 1 · why
fields.text: Say it flatly, once. The doors bolting is doc (Sesh 5) — it doesn’t need justifying, it needs to be a fact.

fields.label: Fallback 2 · Angelique says
fields.text: Go on then. You’ll just have to walk back past whatever I walked past.

fields.label: Fallback 2 · why
fields.text: Turns the exit into a worse choice than the corridor, and gives her a first line that withholds instead of explaining.

fields.label: Scene title
fields.text: First vampire encounter

fields.label: Body
fields.text:
Sesh 8 scripts this beat end to end. Play the vamps as hosts doing a job they agreed to: they think this is the big scare that saves their house, they have no idea anyone has ever died here, and they know the doors are shut because Poe Boy sold the lock-in to them as part of the show — a whole night of terror makes a far better story than five minutes.

Sesh 8 — Bix beat one of three: they catch Edward glimmering in the moonlight. It's the Twilight joke and it's also the first frame of a reveal. Don't hang anything on it; let it be the silly one. Nobody at the table should suspect it matters yet.

1. Hide. Angelique pulls them down. Stealth.
2. The overheard argument. Every line true, every line damning.
3. Explore under recurring stealth checks — eventually someone rolls badly.
4. Dracula swoops in and grapples, pushes, shoves. Enjoys it far too much. No damage.
5. Orlok arrives and ends it with one word. Dracula stops instantly and nobody speaks until Orlok is finished. That one syllable is the entire hierarchy.
6. He dismisses them.

fields.label: Bridge · read-aloud cue
fields.text: “The night is young. It would be terribly rude to be finished with you already.” … “Go on. Have a look around. We'll find you when we're ready.”

fields.label: Bridge · DM note
fields.text:
Every word of that is both a threat and an accurate description of a haunted-house attraction. He means the show has hours left and they'll be back to frighten them again; the party hears exactly one thing, and their next move is to tear the house apart looking for a way out — which is precisely where you want them.

Do not let Orlok discover the locked doors or explain anything. Both hand the party information and let them start reasoning about a third party. He is calm, he decided the doors, and he owns the building.

The read you want is prey given a head start. Same behaviour, two meanings: from the vampires' side it's an attraction — appear, frighten, withdraw, let them keep moving. From the party's side that is exactly what being hunted looks like. “Have our meals been fed?” is the animals, and the party will hear an appetite with a clock on it.

The vampires cannot kill a PC here or in phase one — grapple, shove, frighten, never Bite (the 24 Aug doc paste). The mechanics are the clue: afterwards the players can work out the monsters never once rolled damage.

fields.label: Fallbacks · label
fields.text: If a thread doesn't land

fields.label: Fallback 1 · Anyone with the clipping says
fields.text: You've got the records-hall page in your bag. It says coffins. One of them just said the cellar.

fields.label: Fallback 1 · why
fields.text: Connects the town half to the house half out loud, for the player who wasn't listening in the library.

fields.label: Fallback 2 · Angelique says
fields.text: Three in the morning. That's when it's supposed to happen — that's what he told me.

fields.label: Fallback 2 · why
fields.text: Puts the flyer's 3AM on a timer without her admitting anything yet.

fields.label: Script · DRACULA
fields.text: Five. He said five, and there are five. The boy's finally learning to count.

fields.label: Script · EDWARD
fields.text: One of them is a child.

fields.label: Script · DRACULA
fields.text: They're all children. That's rather the point.

fields.label: Script · ORLOK
fields.text: Have our meals been fed?

fields.label: Script · DRACULA
fields.text: Not yet I don't think.

fields.label: Script · ORLOK
fields.text: See to it before we begin. I won't have them distracted.

fields.label: Scene title
fields.text: The rest of Saturday night

fields.label: Body
fields.text:
Explore again — the search for a way out, the ballroom door nobody answers, the vampires glimpsed at the end of halls and gone when anyone gets there. Doors shut behind them, stairs are blocked, routes narrow. The party will feel driven and won't be able to prove it.

Then Saturday's one combat, late: the botched summoning. Something Poe Boy called up and couldn't put down, sealed in a room upstairs and left there. Its job is proving the house will actually hurt them after an evening in which nothing has — and it quietly plants that the dangerous things in this building are human-made, which is the thesis the computer room pays off on Sunday.

Sesh 8 — Bix beat two of three: they find Edward spying on them, and specifically watching Bix. Play it as a horror beat first: the party's read should be the vampire has picked one of us. Let them be wrong about it for as long as possible. Edward does not explain himself tonight — that's the epilogue, and holding it is what makes it land.

fields.label: Bridge · read-aloud cue
fields.text: End of session one. Everyone levels to 4.

fields.label: Bridge · DM note
fields.text: Everything on Sunday is built for five level-4 PCs. The summoning ends the session on adrenaline. The corridor set-piece is cut (Sesh 8), so Sunday opens on investigation rather than a fight.

items.title: 7. The study, and the party room
items.subtitle: Sunday morning

fields.label: Scene title
fields.text: The study, and the party room

fields.label: Body
fields.text:
The corridor set-piece is cut. Sunday opens on the two per-PC rooms instead.

The study — sealed since the thirties. Inside: a poker set exactly one chip short, the last hand still on the table, and a strongbox holding the deed and the signed Articles of Settlement with the bearer clause spelled out. Run it before anything exonerates the vampires, so Gnomey discovers he owns a house full of things he still believes are killers, and has all of Sunday to sit on it.

The party room — the night Edward and Goblinenon's cart broke down and they found two vampires partying. Bottles, a record still on the turntable, forty years of dust on somebody's good night. Bix finds the photograph here: four figures, two vampires mugging, a pregnant goblin laughing, and a fae with no fangs.

Bix beat three, and the payoff of the other two. Hand the photograph over and say nothing. Bix's player does the arithmetic in front of everybody — a pregnant goblin, in this house, roughly his age ago, standing next to a man who is still here. The prop is live at /photo/; there is writing on the back in her hand.

fields.label: Bridge · read-aloud cue
fields.text: He's read it three times. The name on the deed is his.

fields.label: Bridge · DM note
fields.text:
Make sure Gnomey is alone when he finds it. The arc is quiet-and-overlooked to head of household, and its climax is not the discovery — it's walking back into a room full of people who have never looked at him and saying it out loud. For that to land he needs a stretch where he could have chosen not to. Give Julia the secret and let her decide when to spend it.

How the party gets through the door is deliberately undefined (Scott, 31 Aug). The room and everything in it is Sesh 8; the door is not designed yet. The only constraint worth respecting when you do design it: it has to be a whole-party problem, so that five people open the room and one of them finds out what it means.

fields.label: Bridge · open question
fields.text: Still blank: Cody's and John's rooms. Gnomey has the study, Bix has the party room, Simone's thread lands at the computer — two PCs have nothing.

fields.label: Fallbacks · label
fields.text: If nobody connects the chip

fields.label: Fallback 1 · The set says
fields.text: Forty-nine chips. There's a gap in the tray where the fiftieth should be, and it's the exact size of the one that's been in your pocket all weekend.

fields.label: Fallback 1 · why
fields.text: Physical, not deductive. Put the gap in front of them.

fields.label: Fallback 2 · The contract says
fields.text: “Title shall rest with the bearer of the marker. The marker being the blue one. We agreed on the blue one.”

fields.label: Fallback 2 · why
fields.text: The one paragraph on that page with no corrections in it. Read it aloud and stop.

items.title: 8. The Spirit, the backpack, the USB
items.subtitle: The old rig upstairs

fields.label: Scene title
fields.text: The Spirit, the backpack, the USB

fields.label: Body
fields.text:
The room the kid ran into and never left. Poe Boy's original setup — gear, a mic, and a computer somehow still on, hot-wired off the neighbouring property like everything else in this house. He hasn't been back in here since that night. The AIM prop is live at /aim/.

He was lured by a fake screen name, chased by vampires who believed he was a mall scout, and soul-caged when Poe Boy saw the AIM window open and pulled the door shut. He can name his killer, and he was killed by a human.

fields.label: Bridge · read-aloud cue
fields.text: “my bag is still in this room. by the desk under the coats. can you get it”

fields.label: Bridge · DM note
fields.text:
0 · They have to log in first. The machine sits at an AIM sign-on screen with the account already saved — DJPoeBoy187, because Sesh 7 says this is his computer — and an empty password box. Hand them the sticky note. The password is Fluffy123, his cat, and the prop takes it in any capitalisation so a fat-fingered capital doesn't cost you the scene. Wrong answers get the real AIM error and nothing else: no hints, no lockout, unlimited tries.

They spend this entire conversation typing as the killer. Every line they send arrives under his handle, and the opening is written for it: the boy sees that name come online and comes apart before he works out it isn't him. What saves it is rhythm — “youre not typing like him” — five years of listening to one person at a keyboard. He stops short of naming him as the murderer; he's frightened of a handle, which could just be a bully. The accusation still lands later, in its own beat.

The bag has two things in it, and the order matters.

1 · The wishing willow (Sesh 8). The little wooden token Simone sold him when they were both twelve. He wrote I want Angelique to notice me on it, and it worked — which is the whole reason Angelique knew him well enough to be handed a keyboard. Play his account of it flat and slightly embarrassed. Simone's player will get there first.

2 · The thumb drive. They plug it into the machine and it mounts under his name — that is how the dead kid finally gets one, read off a screen by a player rather than delivered as a lore dump. You two still need one word. The AIM prop takes it as ?name= in the URL, so you can set it from the iPad mid-session without editing anything.

Then he uploads scream_test_03_GOOD.wav over AIM's real file-transfer window — Poe Boy named that file, and the kid has had to look at it every time the monitor wakes up. First ask: expose him. Hand the players an actual USB stick here.

3 · Then the second ask — can you get me out of here. Somewhere safe; the little drive; he doesn't need much room. The goat appears — he can see it and Simone can't — and the price is the piggy bank. The goat joins the chat. The prop turns into a group chat when it arrives — the theme flips dark, the sounds distort, and it negotiates on screen in front of everyone. Then it parks on the hold node so you can play the piggy bank at the table. Three buttons are waiting: she paid, what happens if we get it wrong, and she said no.

⛔ Nothing plot-critical is behind this. The recording, the name and the drive are all already theirs before he asks. A no costs them nothing but him — the machine simply goes dark at sunrise, and they still win the night. Do not fudge it if she declines.

fields.label: Bridge · open question
fields.text: The two setups matter here: this is the old rig upstairs, and the aux he needs is on the ballroom decks downstairs. The USB is the thing that bridges them, which is exactly why the finale's objective is a journey across the map.

fields.label: Fallbacks · label
fields.text: If they don't think to ask what he needs

fields.label: Fallback 1 · The Spirit says
fields.text: “theres something. its stupid but theres something.”

fields.label: Fallback 1 · why
fields.text: He offers rather than waiting to be asked. He has had years to work out what he wants and he is not going to risk them logging off first.

fields.label: Fallback 2 · Anyone says
fields.text: The bag under the coats has a name on it in marker. It's been there long enough that the marker has gone brown.

fields.label: Fallback 2 · why
fields.text: If nobody engages with him, put the backpack in front of them physically. The name does the work on its own.

fields.label: Fallback 3 · The Spirit says
fields.text: “theres something standing behind her. its been in this room the whole time. i dont think she can see it.”

fields.label: Fallback 3 · why
fields.text: If the party takes the file and moves to leave, he raises the second ask himself — and routes it through the one player who can act on it.

fields.label: Scene title
fields.text: The food-stash puzzle

fields.label: Body
fields.text: A puzzle reveals the vampires' food stash — the surprise being it's small animals, not people. Solving it releases a key to a hidden room. This is the proof that clears the vamps.

fields.label: Bridge · read-aloud cue
fields.text: It’s three in the morning — and every speaker in this house just came on at once.

fields.label: Bridge · DM note
fields.text: The flyer’s 3AM is from Sesh 6; using it as the fight’s starting gun is a codex idea, and a good one — it puts a clock on the whole second half from the moment they read the flyer. Because only five people were invited, Poe Boy knows exactly who is in his house, so the show can open by naming them. The bolted doors are the only thing holding them here.

fields.label: Bridge · open question
fields.text: Settled 25 Aug: the 7PM card was exclusive, but the 3AM flyer is public — so this is the moment the house stops being empty. The speakers come on and the guests arrive at the same time. Poe Boy still knows exactly who the five are and can open the show by naming them; the difference is that now there are people to name them in front of. It also answers what he told the vampires: he didn't lie about the houseful, he staggered it.

fields.label: Fallbacks · label
fields.text: If they’d rather hide than go and find him

fields.label: Fallback 1 · The speakers says
fields.text: It’s his voice. And he’s saying your names.

fields.label: Fallback 1 · why
fields.text: Only works because the guest list is five. Hiding stops being an option the second the house addresses them personally.

fields.label: Scene title
fields.text: Climax — three phases

fields.label: Body
fields.text:
Venue: the ballroom / great hall, rigged as a stage. Poe Boy's decks are here; the speakers he's run through the rest of the house are what come on at 3AM. Sesh 7's control idea is settled as manipulation, not mind control — he tells the vampires the party are the mall company's people, the same lie that got the kid killed.

The crowd arrives with the show (settled 25 Aug). The party has been alone in this house for eight hours; at three it fills up, and every beat of the collapse has an audience.

fields.label: Bridge · read-aloud cue
fields.text: Stop after the developer goes down. Let the room be quiet for a moment.

fields.label: Bridge · DM note
fields.text: He is the only death in the story and the only one who isn't a monster. It's self-defence — he sealed them in and attacked first — but these are teenagers, and the comedy that's coming does not start until this has had its silence. The whiplash is genre-correct; it only works if the serious thing lands first.

fields.label: Phase 1 · heading
fields.text: Phase 1 — the vampires attack

fields.label: Phase 1 · body
fields.text: On Poe Boy's lie, believing they are defending their home. Not a balanced encounter — three CR 5 vampires is 5,400 XP against a 2,500 ceiling. It's a two-or-three round pressure scene, and they still cannot kill a PC.

fields.label: Phase 2 · heading
fields.text: Phase 2 — the developer breaches

fields.label: Phase 2 · body
fields.text: He seals the exits behind him, his own crew included. Three sides, nobody sharing a goal. The only lethal fight of the finale. The vampires start tearing into his men — the cue that the room has changed. Poe Boy tries to recruit him and gets brushed off by an adult with a clipboard.

fields.label: Phase 3 · heading
fields.text: Phase 3 — the booth

fields.label: Phase 3 · body
fields.text: The developer dies; the vampires turn, with no persuasion check, because the party killed the man taking their home in front of them. Party plus three vampires against Poe Boy and Lil Stinky. Objective: get the USB to the decks and get on aux.

fields.label: Scene title
fields.text: The collapse

fields.label: Body
fields.text: Stinky stands on the decks; his Aura of Protection is buffing Poe Boy's saves, so he's a puzzle rather than a wall — and he isn't charmed, he just believes his friend. Poe Boy spends his turns on Command — “Drop.” — to keep the drive off the deck: a delay, not a fail state, and the USB can't be destroyed. Then it plays, in full, and the party switches from attacking to defending.

fields.label: Bridge · read-aloud cue
fields.text: Headlights swing across the ballroom windows. Someone has pulled into the drive.

fields.label: Bridge · DM note
fields.text: In order: the recording plays whole — typing, a door, screaming, and under it Poe Boy's own voice staying calm and adjusting a level. Stinky's oath breaks with no saving throw (Devotion's first tenet is don't lie or cheat); he stops fighting and sits down. Silence, one boo, then the whole room. Dracula seizes the mic and denounces him magnificently — he has waited all night for a real audience — and a good number of them still aren't sure it isn't part of the show. Poe Boy tries to Command his way clear and it doesn't land. Then: a Volvo, two sweet oblivious parents in matching fleece, and “Upton, honey?” Sesh 3's throwaway joke about his real name turns out to be load-bearing.

fields.label: Bridge · open question
fields.text: Minor and worth deciding: how does the crowd get in at 3AM when the doors bolted at 7PM? The obvious answer is that Poe Boy opens the front for his own show — but say it out loud, because it touches what the bolt actually means for the party.

fields.label: Scene title
fields.text: Resolution & bookend

fields.label: Body
fields.text:
They recover an ancient Dutch artifact (found after the boss fight, or with the vamps' help), the real-estate company is scared off the land, and they present the artifact in class — closing the loop opened in scene one.

Play the presentation battered. Scott's comment on this beat: “They have scars and black eyes and theyre like ‘and yeah that was our class project’.” Nobody in the room reacts to the state of them, which is the whole joke — let a player deliver the line rather than narrating it.

the finale paste's three closers. Lil Stinky records a diss track — sincere, terrible, devastating. The mega mall breaks ground somewhere else; the brochure says Amityville, quiet neighborhood, waterfront, great bones. And what they actually present is the tape, because the assignment wanted a primary source.

Sesh 8's three epilogue beats:
· Edward explains himself to Bix. The whole timeline — the cart, the party, Goblinenon, the men the company sent, and why he carried a baby down the hill instead of keeping him. Give this its own scene and no jokes in it.
· Poe Boy's mother grounds him in the driveway, and he is certainly not going to that satan concert. The tickets go to Simone, who spent every dollar she had a few hours earlier — and who did not earn these and cannot pay for them.
· The kid gets uploaded to the library computers, where he helps people find new books to read. The boy who died in a room nobody visited spends his afterlife in the busiest building in town.

fields.label: Heading
fields.text: Orlok builds the house

fields.label: Beat 1
fields.text: Orlok built the mansion. Never married, no children, alone in forty rooms — Sesh 6's description of the original owner, now spent on a character who is already in the story.

fields.label: Beat 2
fields.text: He was dying by his own hand when Dracula turned up uninvited and wouldn't take no for an answer. The one he cannot stand is the one he owes his existence to.

fields.label: Beat 3
fields.text: The town buried a man who never left.

items.title: Vinny, the cellar, and the card game
items.subtitle: c.1920 – 14 Nov 1931

fields.label: Heading
fields.text: Vinny, the cellar, and the card game

fields.label: Beat 1
fields.text: Vinny Soprano — Gnomey's great-uncle — runs untaxed cigarettes and bootleg liquor on the back roads at night.

fields.label: Beat 2
fields.text: He needs somewhere to keep the liquor, and there's exactly one building in the county nobody would ever search. He walks up the hill and asks, which nobody has done in two hundred years.

fields.label: Beat 3
fields.text: The deal: Orlok gets the cellar filled and takes a case a month off the top. Liquor turns out to be one of the only human things that still works on a vampire — the one pleasure he has left.

fields.label: Beat 4
fields.text: Every month Vinny comes up with the delivery, they crack a bottle, and they play cards. For decades.

fields.label: Beat 5
fields.text: 14 November 1931. Orlok is down, keeps playing to get it back, and goes further down. By four in the morning the only thing left worth anything is the house, and he puts it up. Drunk and in the hole, they draft the Articles of Settlement — and title rests with the bearer of the marker, one blue chip, for eleven dollars and forty cents.

fields.label: Beat 6
fields.text: Vinny lets them stay. Rent-free, in writing, forever. Collected, then did the decent thing.

fields.label: Beat 7
fields.text: They never speak again. Not from hatred — from shame. You don't visit somebody you've taken from. Repeal comes in '33 and Vinny never comes back for the crates either.

fields.label: Beat 8
fields.text: Years later he hears a twelve-year-old relative had a racket going and torched it rather than eat a skim. He drives over that week, presses the chip into the kid's palm, and never explains what it is. “You'll get another one.”

fields.label: Heading
fields.text: The house and the buyers

fields.label: Beat 1
fields.text: Dood Mansion has sat boarded and empty on the edge of town for as long as anyone can remember — haunted according to rumor, worthless according to everyone else.

fields.label: Beat 2
fields.text: A real-estate company wants to demolish it and build a mega mall.

fields.label: Beat 3
fields.text: They've knocked on the door in daylight several times. The vampires can't answer and can't defend themselves — burning in the sun and all.

items.title: How Edward got here — and how Bix did
items.subtitle: Years before any of it

fields.label: Heading
fields.text: How Edward got here — and how Bix did

fields.label: Beat 1
fields.text: The house was originally just Orlok and Dracula.

fields.label: Beat 2
fields.text: On a rainy night Edward and Goblinenon — Bix's mother — were travelling through town when their cart popped a tire. They stopped at the nearest big house to ask for help, and found two vampires having a party. Rocky Horror, essentially.

fields.label: Beat 3
fields.text: They had such a good time that they ditched the nomadic life and squatted in the abandoned house with the vamps.

fields.label: Beat 4
fields.text: About nine months of partying later, Bix was born.

fields.label: Beat 5
fields.text: Around that time the real-estate company hired men to clear out the squatters and the vampires. Goblinenon was killed in the process and Edward was badly injured. To save his life, the vampires turned him.

fields.label: Beat 6
fields.text: He woke up a vampire, was horrified at what he now was, and carried the baby down into town in the middle of the night. Bix would have a better life than being raised by a single father who was a monster.

fields.label: Beat 7
fields.text: Which makes the company that wants this land the reason Bix is an orphan — and the vampires the reason he has a father at all.

items.title: The willow, and why Angelique still notices
items.subtitle: Five years ago

fields.label: Heading
fields.text: The willow, and why Angelique still notices

fields.label: Beat 1
fields.text: The kid paid Simone for a love spell. She sold him a wishing willow; he wrote I want Angelique to notice me on it.

fields.label: Beat 2
fields.text: It worked. Angelique noticed him — which is exactly why, when Poe Boy needed someone who knew this kid well enough to flirt convincingly over AIM, she was the one who could do it. She played along.

fields.label: Beat 3
fields.text: Nobody ever cancelled it. She still notices him, and the boy it points at isn't anywhere — so what she feels is a pull toward the house he is actually in. That's what she's following the night of the party.

fields.label: Beat 4
fields.text: The spell only ever made her notice. It didn't make her cruel, it didn't type for her, and it didn't drive her out here. She stays fully on the hook for all of that.

fields.label: Beat 5
fields.text: The willow is still in his backpack in the room upstairs.

items.title: How Poe Boy met the vampires
items.subtitle: The alliance

fields.label: Heading
fields.text: How Poe Boy met the vampires

fields.label: Beat 1
fields.text: DJ Poe Boy first went to the house to sample spooky noises for his horror score, and stumbled onto the vamps.

fields.label: Beat 2
fields.text: They tried to scare him off. He wasn't scared — he's jaded, and he studies the occult.

fields.label: Beat 3
fields.text: Things start friendly. He comes over, samples, they talk. Eventually the vamps ask him if there's anything he can do about the real-estate agency.

fields.label: Beat 4
fields.text: He figures that if they can scare people badly enough, nobody will come near the house again.

fields.label: Heading
fields.text: The test run

fields.label: Beat 1
fields.text: Before committing to a whole houseful, Poe Boy tests it on one person — a kid from school.

fields.label: Beat 2
fields.text: Fake screen name on AIM: flirting, then a dare. Go into Dood Mansion at night and prove you're not scared. Angelique types some of the messages. She thinks it's a prank.

fields.label: Beat 3
fields.text: Poe Boy tells the vamps a scout from the real-estate company is coming up the hill. They scare him exactly the way they'd all agreed to.

fields.label: Beat 4
fields.text: It works. And then he notices the thing that ruins him: the more frightened the kid gets, the better the audio.

fields.label: Beat 5
fields.text: The kid finally breaks for the one room with a light on — Poe Boy's setup. Gear, a mic, a computer. (The machine is Poe Boy's, hauled up there to record and edit. It's why there's a working computer in an abandoned house.)

fields.label: Beat 6
fields.text: He isn't planning to do anything about it — not until he reaches the doorway and sees the AIM window open and the kid already typing. That's the turn. He pulls the door shut and holds it.

fields.label: Beat 7
fields.text: The kid is alone in there with a microphone a few feet away, typing for help and screaming at the same time. It's the best audio he's ever gotten. And he can't get caught.

fields.label: Beat 8
fields.text: He panics and reaches for the occult he'd only been reading about — a soul cage, cast badly, with no vessel prepared.

fields.label: Beat 9
fields.text: The nearest thing holding the kid is the machine that's still recording him. It takes all of him. Soul, body, everything.

fields.label: Beat 10
fields.text: He tells the vamps the kid got out that way. As far as the vampires know: the scare worked, a company scout ran off into the woods, and nobody died.

fields.label: Heading
fields.text: The plan they're running now

fields.label: Beat 1
fields.text: Poe Boy and the vamps devise the real plan — the biggest, scariest haunted house they can stage. Scare everyone so badly they'll never come near the house again, and the buyers leave them alone.

fields.label: Beat 2
fields.text: But Poe Boy has other plans. He intends to lock them in, torture them, and sample their screams.

fields.label: Heading
fields.text: What Angelique knows

fields.label: Beat 1
fields.text: Angelique is at home for all of it. She never goes near the mansion that night and never learns the kid died.

fields.label: Beat 2
fields.text: Weeks later she notices he's stopped coming to school. She knows what she helped write, and she starts to suspect what it was for.

fields.label: Beat 3
fields.text: She can't say it out loud — accusing Poe Boy means admitting her part. So she goes to the mansion the night of the party to find out for herself.

fields.label: Beat 4
fields.text: That's why she's already inside when the players get locked in.

fields.label: Day title
fields.text: Saturday · Session 1

fields.label: Subtitle
fields.text: Town & the threshold · level 3

fields.label: First ~third–half · heading
fields.text: Town — and Saturday's fight

fields.label: First ~third–half · body
fields.text: Class recap, the locker cards, the Hall of Records and the gazebo. The trap in the bound volume is the weekend's Saturday combat (500 XP), and springing it is what summons Ostrander to the house that night. Reverses the finale paste's combat-free town.

fields.label: Evening · heading
fields.text: Into the mansion

fields.label: Evening · body
fields.text: The boards are off the front door. They walk in, and the doors bolt. Angelique finds them. First vampire contact — no fight, and mechanically they cannot kill. Opening puzzles.

fields.label: Late · heading
fields.text: The botched summoning

fields.label: Late · body
fields.text: Saturday's one mansion fight — something Poe Boy called up and couldn't put down. Roughly 40 minutes. Its job is proving the house will actually hurt them, and it plants that the dangerous things here are human-made. Then level 3 → 4.

items.title: Sunday · Session 2
items.subtitle: One line, no fork, straight to 3AM · level 4

fields.label: Day title
fields.text: Sunday · Session 2

fields.label: Subtitle
fields.text: One line, no fork, straight to 3AM · level 4

fields.label: Opening · heading
fields.text: The study & the party room

fields.label: Opening · body
fields.text: The corridor set-piece is cut. Sunday opens on the two per-PC rooms: Gnomey finds the deed, the settlement and a poker set one chip short; Bix finds the photograph. Run the study before anything clears the vampires.

fields.label: Middle · heading
fields.text: The Spirit & the USB

fields.label: Middle · body
fields.text: The AIM prop in the old rig upstairs. The backpack — the wishing willow and the drive — the name on the mounted drive, the upload. Hand the players a real USB stick. Then the second ask and Simone's price, which is optional and must stay optional. Then the cellar: the food-stash puzzle clears the vampires, and Vinny's crates are still down there from 1933.

fields.label: Late · heading
fields.text: 3AM — three phases

fields.label: Late · body
fields.text: The ballroom. Vampires hostile, the developer breaches and dies, then the decks. One continuous sequence with no break in it.

fields.label: Close · heading
fields.text: The collapse & bookend

fields.label: Close · body
fields.text: Gnomey's claim and the renewal, Dracula's mic, the Volvo, “Upton, honey?”, grounded, no satan concert, tickets to Simone. Then the epilogue: Edward explains himself to Bix, the kid goes onto the library computers. Monday: the diss track, Amityville, the tape in class — and a phone call to a nursing home.

fields.label: Encounter title
fields.text: The trap in the binding

fields.label: Body
fields.text: The volume is intact when the records keeper hands it over. Opening it springs the developer's trap: the reading room's stationery gets up, and a pair of archival shears ignore the party entirely and go for the article. By the time the shears are down, the page is in pieces — which is where the torn-page prop comes from.

fields.label: Balance verdict
fields.text: Below the low line on purpose — the party spends most of its actions body-blocking rather than attacking, so it plays harder than it reads. A second swarm takes it to 600 if you want more pressure.

fields.label: DM note
fields.text:
The shears don't attack people. Every turn they move for the article and cut; they only hurt someone who physically interposes. They're also the only cutting things in the room, so it is never ambiguous which enemies matter.

Two shears means two approach lanes, and the party has to cover both with bodies. Killing one halves the pressure immediately, which hands them a target priority without you naming it.

The first cut is the trigger, not an action — they come out of the spine as the trap fires, before initiative. The page always gets cut at least once, with no fudging.

Count the cuts; that's the puzzle. The prop opens on a setup screen — tap the bracket and hand the iPad over. One or two cuts → 9 pieces, three or four → 16, five or more → 25. The timer is gone: nothing is resisting them any more, so it's a jigsaw, and the difficulty they earned in the fight is the whole tension.

It contains and erases; it does not kill. He's a businessman scrubbing a stigmatised property, not a murderer, and he wouldn't leave something lethal in a public library. That's what makes him frightening eight hours later, when he is willing.

fields.label: Math · Budget · 5 PCs at level 3

fields.text: 2024 DMG XP budgets. The group-size multiplier is gone — you spend raw monster XP, so 2014-era calculators will build the wrong fight. Cross-check with the Lazy Encounter Benchmark: below 5th level an encounter may be deadly if total monster CR exceeds a quarter of the summed character levels, and a solo monster may be deadly if its CR exceeds the party's average level.

A solo CR 5 against five level-4 PCs is 1,800 XP — under the 2,500 high line, so the DMG calls it undertuned; the benchmark calls it over the solo cap. Both are right: a lone CR 5 isn't hard, it's swingy. It either novas down in two rounds or crits someone to death. The fix in every case below is minions, not hit points.

fields.label: 1. The fampier — the load-bearing clue
fields.text:
Dutch folklore has almost no vampires. The one real find, from a Frisian folklore site:

> **Vampire (Fampier) (Friesland):** Vampires do not typically feature in Dutch folklore;
> nevertheless, in 1973, the Frisian skipper Steven de Bruin recounted a legend concerning
> children who were found dead on the heath, bearing the imprint of teeth upon their throats.
> A "devil-banisher" discovered a fresh corpse buried in the ground at that very spot. He
> declared: "This is the evil that has been found upon the heath." He placed the body inside
> a new coffin, positioning a wooden splinter within the lid so that it pointed directly at
> the corpse's heart. As they nailed the coffin shut, they heard a terrible howling and
> wailing emanating from within. The corpse was buried once more and could do no further
> harm. (See also the *champier* and the *bloedsûger*.) — Poortinga, *Skaakspul* 258

Spencer's read: this gives **the method for defeating them** — dig up the coffins holding
the vampires' bodies, stake through the heart, rebury.

⚠️ **the 24 Aug doc paste cut the fork**, so this is no longer the payoff of a branch. Its job now is to send the
party into the mansion believing they will have to kill three vampires — which makes the reveal land
harder, because they walk in armed with a method and walk out having never needed it.

items.title: 2. The Frisian Kingdom — the setting/period texture

fields.label: 2. The Frisian Kingdom — the setting/period texture
fields.text:
Spencer: "the setting for where the stories take place… we can reference it for making
materials/interactives."

- The ancient **Frisii** lived in the low country between the Zuiderzee and the River Ems.
- Pre-Migration Period (before ~AD 300), the Frisii and the related Chauci, Saxons and Angles
  held the continental coast from the Zuyder Zee to south Jutland. Shared material culture,
  so they can't be told apart archaeologically.
- It was long assumed the Frisii abandoned the land and vanished from the record by AD 400 —
  but recent excavations in the dunes of **Kennemerland** show continuous habitation.
- **Malorix and Verritus**, Frisii chieftains, 1st century AD: in **58 AD** they asked the
  Roman emperor **Nero** to cede territory. While waiting, they walked into the **Theatre of
  Pompey** and sat down among the **Roman senators** without being given permission. Nero
  granted them Roman citizenship — and gave the Frisian territory to Rome's allies anyway.

Malorix and Verritus are the most usable thing here: two named historical figures who showed
up somewhere they weren't invited and sat down anyway. That rhymes with the party walking
into the mansion.

items.title: 3. The Gjenganger — the mansion's other haunt (STILL AN OPEN QUESTION)

fields.label: 3. The Gjenganger — the mansion's other haunt (STILL AN OPEN QUESTION)
fields.text:
Scandinavian revenant. Spencer proposed it and ended with "Up to you if we go with it."

> A Gjenganger is a ghost revived from death to purposefully haunt the living. The word
> combines "again" and "ganger" (walker) — "walking again." They look wholly corporeal, not
> at all ghostly. Typically those who died before their time: murder, suicide, another crime
> or accident. Revenge-motivated and extremely vicious. They attack in the dead of night
> while the victim sleeps, pinching them and fleeing; the victim wakes to a strange blue
> spot, a sign of coming sickness and death. They also spread sickness generally — if it
> touches you, even a brush, your flesh begins to slough away as the virus reaches your heart.
> **To prevent one, a person at risk must be buried in a specific way, with a specific runic
> inscription written inside the coffin** so they cannot wake and walk.

Spencer's proposed backstory: the Gjenganger is the **original owner of the mansion** — never
married, no children, isolated himself in the house and eventually killed himself out of
loneliness. That is a big part of why the house was abandoned, separate from the vampire
rumors. It also gives Will's antisocial character a development beat.

Combat plan: it has the advantage at close range, so the counterplay is distance. It guards
the room with the haunted computer.
